channel.title: Reversal King’s Blog
channel.description: RRK marks band-edge reversal structures and momentum extremes directly on your TradingView charts. A charting tool for traders who read price — not a signal service, not advice.

item.title: Donchian Channel Exit Strategies: Midline vs Opposite Band
item.description: Every Donchian exit answers the same question — how much give-back is acceptable in exchange for staying aboard? The three standard exits compared mechanically, with their failure modes named.

item.title: Pullback or Reversal? A Framework for Telling Them Apart
item.description: A pullback is a pause inside a trend; a reversal is a change of the trend itself. The distinction is only useful once it is defined in observable bar structure — here is a working framework, and its honest limits.

item.title: Donchian Channel Settings: What Changing the Length Really Does
item.description: The length parameter is not a tuning knob for better results — it is a choice about what the word "extreme" means on your chart. What N controls mechanically, and why RRK commits to 1,400 bars.

item.title: Using Moving Averages as Dynamic Support and Resistance
item.description: Moving averages do not hold price the way a level does — they slope, and price interacts with them anyway. What "dynamic" support and resistance actually describes on closed bars, how multi-line stacks encode trend context, and where the approach misleads.

item.title: RSI 75: Overbought or Just a Strong Trend?
item.description: An RSI above 75 is not a sell signal — it is a measurement of how one-sided recent trading has been. What the number shows, why it stays pinned in trends, and how to read it without acting on reflex.

item.title: TradingView Indicator Alerts: A Plain-English Setup Guide
item.description: Alerts turn an on-chart tool into a watchtower — but the dialog offers more choices than most traders need and hides one setting that matters more than all the others. A no-code walkthrough of wiring alerts for a custom indicator, and what each option actually does.

item.title: What Does RSI Above 70 Mean in a Strong Trend?
item.description: RSI above 70 means gains have dominated losses across the lookback window by a wide margin. In a strong trend that state can persist far longer than intuition expects — here is what the threshold measures, where 70 came from, and how to read it deliberately.

item.title: Why RRK Waits for the Close: The Anatomy of a Rejection-With-Reclaim Bar
item.description: Intrabar touches are noise; closed-bar structure is information. A bar-by-bar breakdown of the exact conditions RRK requires before it will mark anything at all.

item.title: Reading Donchian Bands for Reversal Context: A Working Framework
item.description: Most traders use Donchian channels for breakouts. The band edges also encode the opposite setup — rejection-and-reclaim structures. Here is how to read them deliberately.
